drhp.business: Enkei Wheels (India) Limited manufactures aluminium alloy wheels for four-wheeler (4W) vehicles in India, serving the domestic automotive industry as a component supplier. The Company is part of the Enkei Group, with Enkei Corporation, Japan as its holding company.
drhp.end_markets: Indian domestic four-wheeler (passenger/other) automotive OEM market
drhp.expansion: During FY2025, the Company completed the upgradation of the MAP 2 facility into the MAT facility, described as the most advanced technical process, which reduces the manufacturing time of 4W wheels; this MAP2 facility will increase production capacity by around 20,000 pieces per month. The Company has also established a new production unit, MAC 5, at its Factory 2 location, which along with the MAP2-to-MAT conversion has enhanced overall production capacity, reduced manufacturing lead times and improved product quality. risks.note: Capacity utilisation across all plants is steadily increasing; as the business environment improves, long-term growth is expected to depend on further capacity expansion beyond the recently added MAC 5 unit and MAP2-to-MAT conversion.
risks.risk: Long-term growth dependent on further capacity expansion (Strategic Risk)

risks.note: Alloy, the primary raw material, accounts for around 55-60% of the Company's overall cost structure, exposing it to supply disruptions and volatility in market prices.

Employee engagement and productivity are crucial to growth; loss of skilled talent through attrition may affect the Company's growth given the need for creativity, innovative thinking and cross-domain expertise.
Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates may expose the Company to transaction and translation risks; monitored quarterly by the Audit Committee.
High-level outstanding debt, particularly during challenging economic conditions, could adversely affect the Company's financial flexibility and business performance.
Customer defaults may pose a significant risk and adversely impact the Company's financial performance.
The Company is governed by various regulations and contractual obligations; any non-compliance may adversely affect its performance.

Rapid expansion of the automotive industry raises concerns around intellectual property protection, data privacy and warranty-related risk allocation, alongside risks such as cyber-attacks, hacking and internal data leakage.

sk.overview: The DRHP frames Dhoot Transmission within India's automotive Electrical and Electronics (E&E) components industry, principally the wiring harness segment for two-wheelers (2W), three-wheelers (3W) and commercial vehicles (CV), alongside adjacent sensors/controllers, automotive switches and power supply cords. This sits within the broader Indian automotive industry (2W/3W/PV/CV/off-highway), which grew from 21.6 million units (FY20) to 28.2 million units (FY26) at a 4.6% CAGR and is projected to reach 35-45 million units by FY31 (6-8% CAGR).
